title: How One Photon Becomes a Cellular Signal

scenes.tts: How can one activated molecule change a whole cell's current without letting its signal spread or run forever? Follow one photon into a rod cell. Its pathway reveals both the power and the cost of amplification.
scenes.caption: How can one activated molecule change a whole cell's current without letting its signal spread or run forever? Follow one photon into a rod cell. Its pathway reveals both the power and the cost of amplification.
scenes.visual: Build the carried 16:9 world and colour map: input GOLD; active relay BLUE; cGMP TEAL; open channels GREEN; shutoff RED. A rod outer segment fills most of the frame. GREEN channel gates line its membrane, with TEAL cGMP dots holding them open. A single GOLD photon crosses the frame toward one labelled rhodopsin block. The current trace at the bottom flows steadily, then waits at a question mark. Keep a small 'schematic' label visible whenever a biological cartoon is shown. All dots drift and the trace crawls while narration continues.
scenes.narration: How can one activated molecule change a whole cell's current without letting its signal spread or run forever? Follow one photon into a rod cell. Its pathway reveals both the power and the cost of amplification.

scenes.visual: Title 'How One Photon Becomes a Cellular Signal' fades in above the still-moving rod world. The photon hovers beside rhodopsin; cGMP dots drift and the current trace continues.

scenes.tts: In darkness, cyclic G M P holds channels open, and ions carry a steady dark current. The photon activates one rhodopsin. It does not add current. It starts a relay that closes some channels, so the existing current dips.
scenes.caption: In darkness, cGMP holds channels open, and ions carry a steady dark current. The photon activates one rhodopsin. It does not add current. It starts a relay that closes some channels, so the existing current dips.
scenes.visual: Zoom to three GREEN channel gates held open by TEAL cGMP dots. Small neutral ion dots stream through. The GOLD photon touches the rhodopsin block, which turns BLUE. A causal arrow grows toward the channels, but the current trace dips only after the relay begins. The trace is labelled 'schematic', not given invented values.
scenes.narration: In darkness, cGMP holds channels open, and ions carry a steady dark current. The photon activates one rhodopsin. It does not add current. It starts a relay that closes some channels, so the existing current dips.

scenes.tts: Active rhodopsin switches on many transducins. Each active transducin activates phosphodiesterase, which destroys cyclic G M P.
scenes.caption: Active rhodopsin switches on many transducins. Each active transducin activates phosphodiesterase, which destroys cGMP.
scenes.visual: The BLUE rhodopsin block branches into several smaller BLUE transducin blocks. Each moves to a labelled phosphodiesterase block. Those blocks begin sweeping TEAL cGMP dots from the channel area while all particles continue moving.
scenes.narration: Active rhodopsin switches on many transducins. Each active transducin activates phosphodiesterase, which destroys cGMP.

scenes.tts: As cyclic G M P falls, some channels close. The current dip is only a small fraction of the dark current. One event has become many downstream events.
scenes.caption: As cGMP falls, some channels close. The current dip is only a small fraction of the dark current. One event has become many downstream events.
scenes.visual: Carry the same rod layout forward. GREEN gates close one by one as their cGMP dots vanish. The current trace dips. A counter at the right expands from one GOLD input tile into a fan of BLUE output tiles; label the counter 'schematic count'.
scenes.narration: As cGMP falls, some channels close. The current dip is only a small fraction of the dark current. One event has become many downstream events.

scenes.tts: Gain is output molecules per input molecule. In a simple unsaturated cascade, total gain is the product of the step gains.
scenes.caption: Gain is output molecules per input molecule. In a simple unsaturated cascade, total gain is the product of the step gains.
scenes.visual: Flatten the biological relay into three large labelled stages across the same frame. Under them, show the lesson's invented equation, 100 × 1 × 100 = 10,000. Mark it 'invented example'. Each factor lights as its stage pulses.
scenes.narration: Gain is output molecules per input molecule. In a simple unsaturated cascade, total gain is the product of the step gains.

scenes.tts: A catalytic step multiplies. A one-to-one handoff contributes no multiplication. The transducin handoff is one-to-one, between two catalytic stages.
scenes.caption: A catalytic step multiplies. A one-to-one handoff contributes no multiplication. The transducin handoff is one-to-one, between two catalytic stages.
scenes.visual: Stage cards transform in place: 'catalytic' widens into several BLUE branches; 'one-to-one' passes one BLUE block unchanged; the last 'catalytic' widens again. The matching factors in the carried equation glow beneath them.
scenes.narration: A catalytic step multiplies. A one-to-one handoff contributes no multiplication. The transducin handoff is one-to-one, between two catalytic stages.

scenes.tts: A catalytic molecule reaches more targets by working faster or remaining active longer. Rate times active lifetime helps set that step's gain.
scenes.caption: A catalytic molecule reaches more targets by working faster or remaining active longer. Rate times active lifetime helps set that step's gain.
scenes.visual: Keep one BLUE catalytic block centred. A horizontal activity timer grows beneath it while the block repeatedly stamps BLUE downstream blocks. First the stamping speeds up; then the timer lengthens. A running on-screen counter rises in each case.
scenes.narration: A catalytic molecule reaches more targets by working faster or remaining active longer. Rate times active lifetime helps set that step's gain.

scenes.tts: Longer activity can also prolong output. But downstream shutoff or feedback can shorten a high-gain output. Size and duration are not locked together.
scenes.caption: Longer activity can also prolong output. But downstream shutoff or feedback can shorten a high-gain output. Size and duration are not locked together.
scenes.visual: Carry the BLUE block and its full timer forward; its timer is not shortened. RED shutoff tabs act on a downstream stage, not on the BLUE block: the output trace still reaches the same peak but falls sooner, showing that size and duration need not move together. A wiring icon and clock icon settle side by side.
scenes.narration: Longer activity can also prolong output. But downstream shutoff or feedback can shorten a high-gain output. Size and duration are not locked together.

scenes.tts: Now compare two invented routes on screen. Both start from one input. Which route produces more final output? Follow every branch, then multiply each route's displayed step gains.
scenes.caption: Now compare two invented routes on screen. Both start from one input. Which route produces more final output? Follow every branch, then multiply each route's displayed step gains.
scenes.visual: Split the relay into an upper and lower route. Show gains only on screen: the upper route has ×100, ×1, ×100; the lower has ×40, ×1, ×40. Animate one GOLD input entering each route, then freeze before final counters appear. Large question: 'Which route produces more?' The factors remain readable; no answer is shown yet.
scenes.narration: Now compare two invented routes on screen. Both start from one input. Which route produces more final output? Follow every branch, then multiply each route's displayed step gains.

scenes.visual: Deliberate thinking pause. Hold both routes and the question. GOLD input tiles pulse slowly; BLUE branch lines shimmer. No output tiles appear.

scenes.tts: The upper route wins because its displayed factors give the larger product. This rule has limits.
scenes.caption: The upper route wins because its displayed factors give the larger product. This rule has limits.
scenes.visual: Compute both products on screen without speaking them. The upper counter shows 10,000; the lower shows 1,600. A bracket marks the larger product. Then the words 'simple model' appear above both routes.
scenes.narration: The upper route wins because its displayed factors give the larger product. This rule has limits.

scenes.tts: Saturation, shared substrates, deactivation, and feedback can make real pathways depart from simple multiplication. Use the product only when the simple counting assumptions fit.
scenes.caption: Saturation, shared substrates, deactivation, and feedback can make real pathways depart from simple multiplication. Use the product only when the simple counting assumptions fit.
scenes.visual: The routes bend through a narrowing 'saturation' gate, a shared-substrate pool, a RED deactivation timer, and a returning feedback arrow. Each complication appears as a question mark, not a quantified claim.
scenes.narration: Saturation, shared substrates, deactivation, and feedback can make real pathways depart from simple multiplication. Use the product only when the simple counting assumptions fit.

scenes.tts: Amplification also magnifies some upstream fluctuations, so weak signals need evidence. Rod researchers separated blank trials from responses and tested their counts against a Poisson distribution.
scenes.caption: Amplification also magnifies some upstream fluctuations, so weak signals need evidence. Rod researchers separated blank trials from responses and tested their counts against a Poisson distribution.
scenes.visual: Return to the rod world. The trace gains a faint moving noise band around it, labelled 'fluctuation'. Several repeated trials stack briefly, with blanks and dips separated but no invented counts. A small 'Poisson test' bracket groups the trial categories.
scenes.narration: Amplification also magnifies some upstream fluctuations, so weak signals need evidence. Rod researchers separated blank trials from responses and tested their counts against a Poisson distribution.

scenes.tts: Every active component needs a stop. Rhodopsin is shut down, and transducin splits bound G T P to switch itself off.
scenes.caption: Every active component needs a stop. Rhodopsin is shut down, and transducin splits bound GTP to switch itself off.
scenes.visual: RED timer rings close around BLUE rhodopsin and transducin blocks. Each block fades only when its own timer completes, and the relay rewinds toward darkness. GREEN channels begin reopening as TEAL cGMP returns.
scenes.narration: Every active component needs a stop. Rhodopsin is shut down, and transducin splits bound GTP to switch itself off.

scenes.tts: A diffusible messenger can also reach unintended targets. Local binding, anchoring, and destruction restrict its useful pool. Anchoring proteins can hold a kinase, its target, and a messenger-destroying enzyme within one neighbourhood.
scenes.caption: A diffusible messenger can also reach unintended targets. Local binding, anchoring, and destruction restrict its useful pool. Anchoring proteins can hold a kinase, its target, and a messenger-destroying enzyme within one neighbourhood.
scenes.visual: TEAL messenger dots spread from a source toward two target zones. One intended BLUE target sits inside a dashed local boundary; a grey unintended target sits outside. Anchors hold the source and intended target close. A nearby RED destruction block removes dots at the boundary. Keep 'schematic' visible.
scenes.narration: A diffusible messenger can also reach unintended targets. Local binding, anchoring, and destruction restrict its useful pool. Anchoring proteins can hold a kinase, its target, and a messenger-destroying enzyme within one neighbourhood.

scenes.tts: Amplification is therefore not free. A strong signal must be stopped and kept near the right targets.
scenes.caption: Amplification is therefore not free. A strong signal must be stopped and kept near the right targets.
scenes.visual: The local TEAL pool pulses while the outside target remains neutral. RED timers and the dashed local boundary glow together. Two labels settle beside the active region: 'stop it' and 'keep it local'.
scenes.narration: Amplification is therefore not free. A strong signal must be stopped and kept near the right targets.

scenes.tts: Return to the photon. Its cascade made a detectable dip because catalytic stages multiplied its effect, and timed shutoff ended the response. In other pathways, local anchoring and destruction can also limit the spread of a diffusible messenger. Those safeguards make amplification useful.
scenes.caption: Return to the photon. Its cascade made a detectable dip because catalytic stages multiplied its effect, and timed shutoff ended the response. In other pathways, local anchoring and destruction can also limit the spread of a diffusible messenger. Those safeguards make amplification useful.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full rod. Replay the causal sequence quickly: GOLD photon, BLUE relay branching, TEAL cGMP falling, GREEN gates closing, current trace dipping. RED timers then expire in order; cGMP returns and gates reopen. No dashed boundary around the rod. On the third sentence, a small separate inset labelled 'other pathways' shows the s10 anchoring and destruction schematic with generic messenger dots (not cGMP). The moving world dims behind the final card.
scenes.narration: Return to the photon. Its cascade made a detectable dip because catalytic stages multiplied its effect, and timed shutoff ended the response. In other pathways, local anchoring and destruction can also limit the spread of a diffusible messenger. Those safeguards make amplification useful.

scenes.visual: Show one line only, centred over the dimmed moving rod world: 'Simple cascades multiply gain; high gain needs shutoff and sometimes insulation.' No title, subtitle, logo, or smaller line.
